text:
Write Java statements for the following:
(a) To assign the cube root of -343 to a variable with the appropriate datatype.
(b) To assign the position of the last occurrence of @ in the String s with the appropriate datatype.
modelAnswer:
(a) double c = Math.cbrt(-343);
(b) int pos = s.lastIndexOf('@');
keyPoints: Math.cbrt() accepts and returns double; it handles negative numbers (unlike Math.pow with fractional exponent)
Math.cbrt(-343) = -7.0 (cube root of -343 is -7)
lastIndexOf(char) returns the last position of the character, or -1 if not found
The return type of lastIndexOf() is int, suitable for array indices

subject: Computer Applications
text:
Name the method of search and state its prerequisite condition. Also name the sorting algorithm that is performed as a prerequisite.
(a) For which the array must be sorted before searching.
(b) What sorting algorithm can be used to sort the array as a prerequisite?
modelAnswer:
(a) Binary Search requires the array to be sorted.
(b) Selection Sort (or any comparison-based sort such as Bubble Sort) can be used.
keyPoints: Binary Search divides the search space in half each iteration — requires sorted array
Binary Search has O(log n) complexity vs Linear Search's O(n)
Selection Sort finds the minimum element and places it in correct position each pass
Bubble Sort is another valid prerequisite sorting algorithm
